item.title: Former Hokkaido Government Office — Guide
item.description: The Former Hokkaido Government Office, affectionately nicknamed ‘Akarenga’ (‘Red Brick’), is one of Sapporo’s most beloved historic landmarks, standing grandly in the heart of the city. Completed in 1888 in an American neo-Baroque style, this imposing red-brick building — made with some 2.5 million locally-fired bricks and topped by an octagonal dome — served as the seat of Hokkaido’s government for about 80 years. It’s a striking symbol of the Meiji-era pioneer spirit and the American influence on the island’s development.

item.title: Sapporo Clock Tower — Guide
item.description: The Sapporo Clock Tower (Tokeidai) is one of the city’s most famous and beloved symbols, a charming wooden building in the American colonial style that dates from Hokkaido’s pioneer development era. Built in 1878 as a drill hall for the Sapporo Agricultural College (the forerunner of Hokkaido University), it was fitted with its distinctive tower clock in 1881 — a mechanism imported from Boston that still keeps time today, making it one of the oldest working tower clocks in Japan.
